newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee stays firm as money rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee stays firm as money rates rise.

text.p: Rising money rates pushed up the Sri Lanka rupee against the dollar as banks sold the U.S. unit to generate local currency, dealers said.
At 0415 GMT the rupee was at 56.95 to the dollar, which was its opening level and also the previous closing rate.
The rupee rose early to a high of 56.85 to the dollar, when the Central Bank pushed down the U.S. unit by 1.75 local cents, and fixed buying and selling prices at 55.9276 and 57.0574.
"The exchange rate has been very volatile in a narrow range as banks sell dollars and create rupees due to high money rates," said a standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money was at 21 percent, which was the highest for the morning, after opening at 17 percent, dealers said.
A big state bank which was borrowing aggressively, caused money rates to remain high, they said.
